scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, value proposition, and CTAs correctly

steps.description: Navigate to the MirDB product homepage
steps.context: User arrives from search, GitHub, or referral

steps.description: Check that product name 'MirDB' and tagline 'Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol' are visible
steps.context: Content should be immediately visible within the first viewport

steps.description: Confirm 'Get Started' primary CTA and 'View on GitHub' secondary CTA are present and clickable
steps.context: CTAs should be prominently displayed in the hero section

test_cases.input: Load homepage and check hero section
test_cases.expected: Product name 'MirDB' is visible in hero section
Tagline 'Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol' is displayed
'Get Started' button is visible and has correct styling
'View on GitHub' button is visible and links to GitHub repository
2-3 sentence description explaining MirDB value proposition is visible

scenarios.name: Key Features Section
scenarios.description: Verify the key features section displays memcached compatibility, persistence, LSM architecture, and simple configuration

steps.description: Navigate past the hero section to the key features area
Check that all four key features are displayed with icons and descriptions
steps.context: Features: Memcached Compatible, Persistent Storage, High Performance, Simple Configuration

test_cases.expected: Feature card displays 'Memcached Compatible' with description about drop-in replacement
Feature card displays 'Persistent Storage' with SSTable architecture description
Feature card displays 'High Performance' with LSM tree optimization description
Feature card displays 'Simple Configuration' with TOML-based configuration description
Each feature card has an associated icon or visual indicator

scenarios.name: Architecture Overview Section
scenarios.description: Verify the architecture section displays LSM tree data flow diagram and explanation

steps.description: Scroll to the architecture overview area of the homepage
Check that a visual diagram showing WAL -> Memtable -> SSTable levels is displayed
steps.context: Diagram should clearly show data flow

steps.description: Check that brief explanation of LSM tree benefits is provided
steps.context: Content should be accessible to technical readers

test_cases.expected: Visual diagram showing data flow (WAL, Memtable, SSTable levels) is rendered
Brief explanation of LSM tree benefits is present near the diagram
Link to detailed architecture documentation is available

scenarios.name: Quick-Start Section
scenarios.description: Verify quick-start section provides installation instructions and usage examples with copyable code blocks

steps.description: Scroll to the quick-start installation area
steps.context: Developer wanting to try MirDB immediately

steps.description: Check that cargo build commands are displayed with copy functionality
Check that SET, GET, DELETE command examples are shown

test_cases.expected: cargo build command is displayed in a code block

test_cases.input: Check copy functionality on code blocks
test_cases.expected: Code blocks have one-click copy buttons that work correctly
SET command example with realistic key-value pair is displayed
GET command example is displayed showing retrieval syntax
DELETE command example is displayed showing deletion syntax
Basic TOML configuration example is provided
Example showing connection using standard memcached client is present

scenarios.name: Protocol Reference Section
scenarios.description: Verify supported commands table and MirDB-specific commands are documented

steps.description: Scroll to the protocol reference area
Check that supported memcached commands are listed in a table
steps.context: Commands: SET, GET, ADD, REPLACE, DELETE, APPEND, PREPEND, GETS

steps.description: Check that INFO and MAJOR_COMPACTION commands are highlighted separately

test_cases.expected: Table listing SET, GET, ADD, REPLACE, DELETE, APPEND, PREPEND, GETS commands is visible
INFO and MAJOR_COMPACTION commands are listed separately with descriptions
Response codes (STORED, NOT_STORED, EXISTS, NOT_FOUND, DELETED, ERROR) are documented

scenarios.name: Configuration Reference Section
scenarios.description: Verify configuration parameters table with default values is displayed

steps.description: Scroll to the configuration reference area
steps.context: Developer setting up MirDB with custom configuration

steps.description: Check that key configuration parameters are listed with default values
steps.context: Parameters include addr, max_level, work_dir, sst_max_size, etc.

test_cases.expected: Table with key configuration parameters (addr, max_level, work_dir) is visible
Default values are shown for each parameter (e.g., addr: 0.0.0.0:12333)
Link to full configuration documentation is available
